observation.visible_scene: A low, water-level view over a calm sea under a bright, hazy sun sitting just above the horizon, with a thin sun-glare reflection streaking the water and a low, dark coastline visible off to one side. The pointed white nose of a board (with a small dark tip) is fixed at the bottom edge of the frame, and a hand occasionally enters the lower-right corner. The sky is filled with soft, streaky clouds.
visible_changes: The white board nose slides across the bottom of the frame from the right corner (frames 1-11) toward the center (12-16), then to the left edge (17-18), leaves the frame (19-26), and re-enters at the left edge (27-41); because the nose is attached to the board, this sweep reflects camera yaw/rotation rather than the board translating across the water.

The sun's reflection and the coastline shift position in step with the board nose (sun moves from center-right to the left side and back toward the right; the landmass disappears from the left horizon and later reappears), consistent with the camera panning/turning relative to the scene.
The horizon line tilts at varying angles through the clip (roughly level early, more diagonal in the middle and at the end), indicating camera roll as well as yaw.
A hand with a small splash of water briefly appears at the bottom-right corner around frames 24-26, then withdraws.
The water surface shows only gentle ripples and the moving glare path; no wave breaking or large wake is visible.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the person is paddling, turning, or simply holding the camera; whether the board is drifting or stationary.
What the hand is doing before it enters and after it leaves the frame.
The direction and intent of the camera pan, and what lies outside the visible horizon.
uncertain_details: The exact cause of the board-nose movement across the frame (camera rotation vs. the board itself turning) cannot be separated from the background motion, since both sweep together.
Whether the coastline seen at the start and the one reappearing at the end are the same landmass viewed from different angles.
The precise moment the pan reverses is not marked by a clear cut; it appears as continuous motion.

the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.

do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.

camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
